### Past-due tax returns information

Many expats don’t realize they’re required to file taxes every year. Fortunately, the IRS offers an amnesty program for expats who haven’t filed taxes in three years or more.

You may qualify for IRS tax amnesty if:

- You confirm that your failure to file U.S. tax returns and FBAR was due to an honest misunderstanding of your responsibilities.
- You’ve lived in a foreign country for at least 330 days during one of the last three years and not maintained a U.S. residence.

## Doing expat tax filing online just got easier

Our software offers guidance as you prepare and file your taxes with all the standard expat forms and schedules, including the Foreign Tax Credit or Foreign Earned Income Exclusion.

Online federal filing software

Filed federal taxes in the U.S.? You’ll likely need to file them abroad. Our expat filing tax software knows how to find the right credits and deductions.

Learn more

State tax return preparation and filing

Depending on your unique situation, you may need to file a state return. If so, you can add this for an extra fee, and our tax tool will help you file.

Learn more

FBAR filing (Report of Foreign Bank and Financial Accounts)

If you’re a U.S. citizen or resident with money in a non-U.S. bank account, our tax tool helps with completing and submitting your forms for compliance.

Learn more

Free extension filing

The IRS grants an automatic two-month extension until June 15 for expat filers. If you need more time, we’ll request an extension until Oct. 15 for free.

Learn more

Past-due returns (IRS Streamlined Procedure)

Our Streamlined Filing Compliance Procedure expertise will help you avoid penalties if you’re behind on expat taxes or FBAR filings.

Learn more

Security and support

Our online software has multiple layers of protection for your sensitive information and unlimited technical support when you need it.
